sources_overview.Spec: ECMA-262 17th edition (ECMAScript 2026, Spec p.25). Official standard; it barely states the edition in which features were introduced, apart from occasional notes and Annexes E (p.865) and F (p.867-869).
sources_overview.EJpt: Eloquent JavaScript PT-BR (504 p.). Declares it uses 'the 2024 version of JavaScript' (EJpt p.9; the 4th edition is an [inference]). It dates only class, Symbol, arrow functions and ES modules to 2015, and var/CommonJS as pre-2015.
sources_overview.EJ1: Eloquent JavaScript (file named EN-3ed, actually the 1st edition from 2007 revised until Nov/2013, EJ1 p.247). Everything in it is [DATED].

items.name: History: ES3, ES4, ES5, ES6 and ES2024/ES2026
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: Historical overview of the versions in EJpt; EJ1 mentions that ES5 is already out and cites 'Harmony' in 2011; the Spec defines the 17th edition (ECMAScript 2026).
items.citations: EJpt p.9; EJ1 p.6; Spec p.25

items.name: class (class syntax)
items.version: ECMAScript 2015 (ES6)
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: Defined since ECMAScript 2015 as a concise form of the constructor + prototype pattern; a class body is always strict mode; calling it without new throws TypeError. Class fields and private # members have no stated version.

items.name: Symbol (primitive type and Symbol function)
items.version: 2015 (stated by EJpt; the Spec does not state the edition)
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: Added in 2015 according to EJpt; unique, immutable values used as collision-free property keys; calling with new throws TypeError.

items.name: Arrow functions (=>)
items.version: 2015 (stated by EJpt; the Spec does not state the edition)
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: Added in 2015 according to EJpt; they have no this, arguments, super or new.target of their own and cannot be called with new.

items.name: ES modules (import / export)
items.version: ECMAScript 2015 (stated by EJpt; the Spec does not state the edition)
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: Since ECMAScript 2015 there are scripts and modules; modules have their own scope and are automatically strict. Loading and specifier resolution are delegated to the host [HOST].

items.name: let and const (block-scoped lexical declarations and TDZ)
items.version: ECMAScript 2015 (var is pre-2015 [DATED])
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: EJpt presents var as the pre-2015 form and let/const with block scope; EJ1 mentions let only as a future promise of 'Harmony'; Annex F records the let grammar in ES2015.

items.name: CommonJS (require / module.exports / exports) and the IIFE pattern
items.version: Pre-2015 [DATED] [HOST]
items.label: [DATED] [HOST]
items.detail: Improvised system predating 2015 based on functions and require; EJpt states there is no longer any reason to write new programs in CommonJS. EJpt uses the `exports` object and the `require` function; `module.exports` and the acronym IIFE do not appear in the sources (EJpt describes the immediately invoked function expression in full, p.225) [extrapolation].

items.name: await (reduced number of Jobs in ES2019) and async/await
items.version: async/await syntax: version not stated in the sources; await Job reduction: ES2019
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: The edition in which async/await entered is not in the sources, but Annex F records that in ES2019 the number of Jobs enqueued by await was reduced, which can change the observable order between then() and await.

items.name: Atomics.notify (renamed from Atomics.wake)
items.version: ECMAScript 2019
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: Atomics.wake was renamed to Atomics.notify in ES2019 to avoid confusion with Atomics.wait.

items.name: Tagged templates (canonicalization of template objects by Parse Node)
items.version: Canonicalization change in ECMAScript 2018 (template literal syntax: entry version not stated)
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: Since ES2018 template objects are canonicalized by Parse Node (location in the source code) and not by all occurrences of the same literal in the Realm.

items.name: Unicode 8.0.0 (U+180E in trim), latest Unicode version and arguments.caller
items.version: ES2016 (Unicode 8.0.0 / U+180E) and ES2017 (latest Unicode; removal of arguments.caller; for-in with initializer in sloppy mode)
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: In ES2016 U+180E stopped being whitespace ('\u180E'.trim().length went from 0 to 1); in ES2017 the Spec started requiring the latest Unicode version, dropped the arguments.caller requirement that threw an error and again allowed for (var x = ... in ...) in non-strict mode.

items.name: Object.freeze / keys / isFrozen / isSealed / isExtensible / getPrototypeOf with primitives
items.version: Change in the handling of non-objects in ECMAScript 2015
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: Before ES2015 they threw TypeError for a non-object argument; since ES2015 they treat primitives as a non-extensible object (freeze/isFrozen/isSealed/isExtensible/preventExtensions/seal) or apply ToObject (keys/getPrototypeOf/getOwnPropertyNames/getOwnPropertyDescriptor).

items.name: Binary and octal literals in ToNumber ('0b101', '0o17') and RegExp flags on the prototype
items.version: ECMAScript 2015 (Annexes E and F)
items.label: [VERSION-DEPENDENT]
items.detail: In ES2015 ToNumber on a String began to recognize '0b' and '0o' (previously NaN); the RegExp source/global/ignoreCase/multiline went from instance properties to getters on RegExp.prototype; Date.prototype and RegExp.prototype stopped being instances of Date/RegExp.

items.name: Operators ?., ??, ??=, &&=, ||=, ** and BigInt / numeric separators _
items.version: version not stated in the sources (present in the ES2026 Spec / EJpt)
items.label: [from source]
items.detail: Defined in the 2026 Spec and used in EJpt, but none of the three sources states in which ECMAScript edition they were introduced.

items.name: Private fields and methods (#x), instance fields and static {} blocks
items.version: version not stated in the sources (present in the ES2026 Spec / EJpt)
items.label: [from source]
items.detail: Private # members and class fields are in the 2026 Spec and in EJpt, and static {} blocks in the 2026 Spec, with no stated entry edition.

items.name: Object.hasOwn, Object.groupBy and Map.groupBy
items.version: version not stated in the sources (present in the ES2026 Spec)
items.label: [from source]
items.detail: Object.hasOwn is in the Spec (p.464) and in EJpt (p.138); Object.groupBy (returns an object with a null prototype, p.464) and Map.groupBy (returns a Map, p.677) are only in the Spec. None has a stated entry edition.

items.name: Array: at, findLast, findLastIndex, toSorted, toReversed, toSpliced, with, fromAsync, flat, flatMap
items.version: version not stated in the sources (present in the ES2026 Spec)
items.label: [from source]
items.detail: Defined in clause 23.1 of the 2026 Spec with no indication of the edition in which they entered.

items.name: Set: union, intersection, difference, symmetricDifference, isSubsetOf, isSupersetOf, isDisjointFrom
items.version: version not stated in the sources (present in the ES2026 Spec)
items.label: [from source]
items.detail: Set algebra operations on Set.prototype; they require a set-like argument (passing a plain Array throws TypeError).

items.name: Iterator, Iterator.from, Iterator.concat and Iterator helpers (map, filter, take, drop, toArray...)
items.version: version not stated in the sources (present in the ES2026 Spec)
items.label: [from source]
items.detail: Defined in clause 27.1 of the 2026 Spec (Spec p.753-761) with no stated entry edition.

items.name: Promise: all, allSettled, any, race, try, withResolvers and AggregateError / Error cause
items.version: version not stated in the sources (present in the ES2026 Spec)
items.label: [from source]
items.detail: Promise and Promise.all are in the Spec and in EJpt; allSettled, any (AggregateError), race, try, withResolvers and the { cause } option of Error are in the Spec with no stated entry edition.

items.name: Float16Array, Math.f16round, Math.sumPrecise, Uint8Array base64/hex, RegExp.escape, JSON.rawJSON
items.version: version not stated in the sources (present in the ES2026 Spec)
items.label: [from source]
items.detail: Present in the 2026 Spec with no information about the entry edition.

items.name: Top-level await, import attributes and JSON modules
items.version: version not stated in the sources (present in the ES2026 Spec; supported attributes are [HOST])
items.label: [from source] [HOST]
items.detail: The Module grammar allows top-level await and ImportAttributes; which attributes the environment accepts depends on the host.

items.name: Annex B: escape/unescape, substr, getYear/setYear/toGMTString, String HTML methods, RegExp.prototype.compile, HTML comments
items.version: Annex B legacy (no stated entry edition)
items.label: [DATED] [HOST]
items.detail: Normative only for browsers and discouraged by the Spec in new code. Prefer slice (instead of substr), getFullYear/setFullYear/toUTCString, trimStart/trimEnd.

items.name: __proto__, __defineGetter__, __defineSetter__, __lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__ and with
items.version: Legacy (Normative Optional / Legacy in the Spec)
items.label: [DATED]
items.detail: __proto__ and the __define/lookup* methods are marked Normative Optional, Legacy (prefer Object.getPrototypeOf / Object.create / Object.defineProperty); 'with' is LEGACY and forbidden in strict mode (SyntaxError).

items.name: Environment APIs [HOST]: DOM, window, document, fetch, setTimeout, console, localStorage, Canvas, Node.js (fs, http, process)
items.version: Defined by the host environment (not part of ECMA-262)
items.label: [HOST]
items.detail: The Spec defines neither input/output nor browser or server APIs, only abstract host hooks (Annex D). EJpt covers DOM, events, fetch, localStorage, Canvas and Node.js (citing Node 18+).

items.name: Outside the sources: TypeScript, React/Vue/Express, Temporal, structuredClone, queueMicrotask, AbortController
items.version: Not covered by the package sources
items.label: [extrapolation]
items.detail: They do not appear in the 2026 Spec or in the two books (TypeScript has only a passing mention in EJpt p.171; Intl is only referenced to ECMA-402 in Spec p.25).
